name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks into a local folder for direct inspection: `mkdir -p ~/mine-ai-look && cd ~/mine-ai-look && git clone https://github.com/eitan-picks/mine-ai-designs.git` (128 MB, 47 files). Then I’ll open the repo in Figma and run a quick `figma-export` CLI to batch-export PNGs at 2× for side-by-side taste tests.

name: Squint
text: Squint here—why assume Eitan’s picks are *current* or *aligned* with Mine AI’s product stage? A 128MB repo cloned blindly risks stale designs, unvalidated taste, or even mislabeled assets. Demand a dated commit hash or a README proving these are the *latest* and *approved* references before exporting. And where’s the task-relative value? Batch-exporting PNGs without filtering for *our* UI’s constraints (e.g., dark mode, responsive grids) is pure waste—show me the criteria for what’s "learnable" vs. noise.
